newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Mixed trading seen persisting in Nigerian shares.
newsitem.headline: Mixed trading seen persisting in Nigerian shares.

text.p: Nigerian share trading is set to remain mixed next week as corporate results and the influence of supply and demand have their full effect, dealers said on Friday.
The all-share index was a touch lower at 8805.48 from 8805.50 on Thursday.
"A sharp drop in after-tax profit by cement giant West African Portland Cement Company (WAPCO) did not surprise many traders but market reaction has been delayed," one said.
WAPCO posted a profit of 1.8 billion naira for the year to end-1996 against 3.1 billion naira a year ago, although turnover rose to 9.2 billion naira from 9.1 billion naira.
"The market will likely react to the result next week when fresh information on the closure of the company's register and payment date for the new dividend is made public," said another.
Prices are also swinging widely on the stock exchange because of the changing fortunes of key stocks, analysts said.

Some bank shares, having risen since January to historic levels, were set to fall on profit taking while oil marketers would continue to attract less attention due to a share glut and dwindling investor interest, they said.

"Many investors are selling their oil shares because they now feel they cannot keep rising forever," said one analyst, adding "Besides, demand for them is not what it used to be. People no longer want them at any price."
A spate of recent fuel shortages has taken the shine off oil stocks, which usually are most sought after on the bourse.
Agip fell 20 kobo to 26.50 naira on Friday as investors continued to sell. But Mobil was up by a similar margin to 61.20 naira.
Afribank rose 20 kobo to 10.00 naira while First Bank and Union Bank slid five kobo and 22 kobo, respectively, to 20.25 naira and 16.70 naira.
Nigerian-German Chemicals, formerly Nigerian Hoechst, closed 50 kobo down at 9.00 naira on adjustment for dividend payment.
Food and beverages stocks will trade firm on increasing demand, dealers said.
Nigerian Bottling Company at 57.10 naira, Nestle at 70.40 naira and Union Dicon Salt at 51.30 naira, were each 10 kobo gainers on Friday.
"These are shares with good prospects in which the market has considerable confidence," one trader said.
